expertInsight: Forecasting and opportunity splits are easier to understand when you build them. Forecasts follow the role hierarchy, and opportunity splits must be enabled before teams can use them. Try the setup in a free Developer org with several users and opportunities. Also practice territory management, especially how moving an account between territories changes access.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Agentforce Sales Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce renamed Sales Cloud Consultant to Agentforce Sales Consultant. The exam is at a moderate level and expects strong administrator knowledge and project experience. Many questions describe a sales team’s needs and ask you to choose a suitable Salesforce setup.
bullets: 60 scored multiple-choice questions, plus up to five unscored, in 105 minutes.
73% to pass. Check the current exam guide before booking.
Consulting counts most. Consulting and Implementation Strategies is the largest section at 25%, ahead of any single product area.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You are ready when you can configure a sales process, use forecasts, and explain how territory management affects access. Aim for at least 85% on three full practice tests. Practice building the configuration in Salesforce as well as reviewing it.

examFormat.heading: Agentforce Sales Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Many questions ask you to choose Salesforce features for a sales team’s workflow.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions use short scenarios. For example, a sales team may need to share credit for a deal or see forecasts by region. Choose the feature that best meets the stated need.
bestWayToPass: Study forecasting: Learn how opportunity stages map to forecast categories, how forecasts roll up through the role hierarchy, and who can adjust them.
Review opportunity management: Understand sales processes, stages, record types, opportunity teams, and splits.
Understand territories: Learn how accounts and opportunities are assigned to territories and how territory membership affects access.
Practice in Salesforce: Set up sample users and records in a Developer Edition org to see how configuration choices work.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers how to design and configure Sales Cloud, from leads and accounts to opportunities, products, quotes, forecasts, territories, and reporting. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 73% pass mark, weighted towards Consulting and Implementation Strategies (25%) and Practical Application of Agentforce Sales Expertise (24%).

keyConcepts.h2: Agentforce Sales Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Leads: Assignment and Conversion
blocks.body: A **Lead** is a potential customer who is not yet qualified. **Lead assignment rules** use field values to route new leads to users or queues. The first matching rule entry applies, so the order matters. A **queue** holds leads that a team can claim. **Web-to-Lead** collects leads from a website form, and **auto-response rules** can send an initial reply. Converting a Lead creates an Account and Contact, and may create an Opportunity. Custom lead fields must be mapped before conversion if their values should move to the new records. **Matching rules** and **duplicate rules** help identify existing records. **Einstein Lead Scoring** ranks leads based on patterns in leads that converted.

blocks.heading: Opportunities, Sales Stages, and Splits
blocks.body: A **sales process** sets the stages available for an Opportunity. It is linked to a **record type**, so different business lines can use different processes. Each stage has a default probability and a **forecast category**. **Opportunity teams** let several users work on one deal with different roles and access. **Opportunity splits** assign portions of a deal to team members: revenue splits must total 100%, while overlay splits can add up to more or less than 100% for people who support the deal. **Products** and **price books** define what is sold and its price. The standard price book is available by default; custom price books can support different markets or channels. **Quotes** can be created from an Opportunity’s products.

blocks.heading: Collaborative Forecasts
blocks.body: **Collaborative Forecasts** roll up Opportunity amounts through the **role hierarchy**, so managers can see their teams’ numbers. They use **forecast categories**, such as Pipeline, Best Case, Commit, and Closed, which are tied to Opportunity stages. Forecasts can use revenue, quantity, product families, splits, or other supported measures, and more than one forecast type can be active at once. Managers can enter **adjustments** while keeping the original rollup visible. **Quotas** can be assigned to users and compared with forecasts. The role hierarchy affects the rollup, so configure it carefully.

blocks.heading: Territory Management
blocks.body: **Enterprise Territory Management** assigns Accounts to territories using rules and gives territory users access to those Accounts and their Opportunities. Teams can create and test a **territory model** in planning state before activating it. Only one model can be active at a time. **Territory types** and hierarchies organize the model, such as by region and then by segment. Assignment can use rules or be done manually. Forecasts can also be organized by territory. Know how reassigning an Account affects access.

blocks.heading: Sales Productivity and Reporting
blocks.body: Salesforce includes features that help sales representatives save time. **Email templates** provide reusable messages, and **Einstein Activity Capture** reduces manual activity logging. **Path** displays guidance for each stage on a record page. **Kanban** lets users move Opportunities between stages. **Sales Engagement** supports call and email cadences. For reporting, understand the difference between a **report type**, a **summary report**, and a **joined report**. A dashboard’s **running user** determines whose data is shown to viewers. Scenario questions may describe pipeline, win-rate, or forecast reports.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Agentforce Sales Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions describe a sales team’s workflow and ask which Salesforce setup meets its needs. Start with the requirement and choose the feature designed for it.

blocks.heading: Follow a Lead Through a Sale
blocks.body: Review lead capture and assignment, conversion to an Account and Contact, optional Opportunity creation, product selection, quotes, and forecasting. Know what conversion creates and how field mapping works.

blocks.heading: Forecasts and Territories
blocks.body: Forecasts roll up through the role hierarchy and use forecast categories. Territories can give users access to Accounts and their Opportunities, and support territory forecasts.

blocks.heading: Opportunity Splits
blocks.body: Revenue splits must add up to 100%. Overlay splits can total a different amount and can represent support from specialists.

blocks.heading: Sales Process Setup
blocks.body: Record types connect to sales processes, which set the available Opportunity stages. Stages have a default probability and forecast category.

blocks.heading: Choose a Report
blocks.body: Summary reports group information. Joined reports show multiple report blocks together. A dashboard’s running user controls whose data viewers see.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants new Leads assigned to sales reps by region. Which feature should it use?
options: Lead auto-response rules
Lead assignment rules
Opportunity team defaults
Territory assignment rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lead assignment rules can assign Leads to users or queues based on criteria such as region, industry, or source.
whyWrong: Auto-response rules send a reply to the person who submitted the Lead; they do not assign an owner.
Opportunity teams apply to deals, not to incoming Leads.
Territory assignment rules place Accounts in territories; they do not route Leads to reps.

sampleQuestions.question: What do Opportunity Splits let a sales team do?
options: Create child Opportunities under a parent deal
Divide one Opportunity into several stages
Share credit for one deal among team members
Track rival vendors bidding on the same deal
sampleQuestions.explanation: Opportunity Splits let a team share credit for one Opportunity. Each member can receive a percentage of the credit.
whyWrong: Splits share credit on one Opportunity; they do not create child records.
Stages show the progress of one Opportunity. Splits do not divide it into stages.
The Competitors related list tracks competitors.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales manager wants a forecast that includes Opportunities from direct reports and people lower in the role hierarchy. Which feature supports this?
options: Opportunity Teams
Campaign Influence
Einstein Lead Scoring
Collaborative Forecasts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Collaborative Forecasts let managers review team forecasts, adjust amounts, and see rollups through the role hierarchy.
whyWrong: Opportunity Teams record who works on a deal; they do not roll up forecast amounts.
Campaign Influence links campaigns to Opportunities; it is not a forecasting feature.
Lead Scoring ranks Leads; it does not produce a team forecast.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Path help users on an Opportunity?
options: Shows key fields and guidance for each sales stage
Sends an email alert each time the stage changes
Moves the deal to the next stage automatically
Calculates the forecast amount for each stage
sampleQuestions.explanation: Path gives users visual guidance at each stage, including key fields and tips for success.
whyWrong: Path shows guidance; it does not send email.
A user changes the stage. Path does not move it automatically.
Path does not calculate forecasts.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a sales process control in Salesforce?
options: Which users are assigned newly created Opportunities
Which Opportunity stages a record type can use
How revenue is calculated on each Opportunity
When Opportunities are created from Leads
sampleQuestions.explanation: A sales process defines which stages are available and is linked to a record type, so different business lines can follow different stages.
whyWrong: Ownership and assignment settings decide who owns an Opportunity.
A sales process defines stages; it does not calculate revenue.
Lead conversion creates Opportunities; a sales process does not.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants to compare sales reps’ Opportunity results this quarter. Which report should they use?
options: Opportunities by Stage
Opportunities by Product
Opportunities by Owner
Opportunities by Account
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Opportunities by Owner report groups deals by the rep who owns each one, so the manager can compare results by rep.
whyWrong: This groups deals by stage, not by rep.
This groups deals by product, not by rep.
This groups deals by customer account, not by rep.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Enterprise Territory Management help a company do?
options: Record the competitors involved in each open Opportunity
Route new Leads to sales queues based on the value of the Lead source field
Calculate commission payments from closed Opportunities
Assign Accounts to territories and give territory users access
sampleQuestions.explanation: Enterprise Territory Management assigns Accounts to territories, using rules or manual assignment, and gives territory users access to those Accounts and their Opportunities.
whyWrong: The Competitors related list tracks competitors.
Lead assignment rules route Leads.
Territory management organizes sales coverage; it does not calculate commissions.

sampleQuestions.question: Three months after go-live, few reps are logging Opportunities. What should the consultant do first?
options: Find out why through user feedback and usage reports
Add validation rules that force reps to fill in more fields
Rebuild the sales process with a new set of record types
Ask managers to remove access from reps who do not log in
sampleQuestions.explanation: Low adoption has many possible causes, such as training gaps or a process that does not match how reps work. Finding the cause comes before changing the configuration.
whyWrong: More required fields can make adoption worse if the cause is not yet known.
Rebuilding before knowing the cause risks solving the wrong problem.
Removing access does not address why reps are not using the system.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the main purpose of a discovery workshop at the start of a project?
options: Train end users on the features that have already been configured
Understand business needs and agree which use cases come first
Migrate legacy data into the production org before design starts
Sign off the final solution so that the build can be deployed
sampleQuestions.explanation: Discovery is where the consultant gathers and documents requirements, then works with stakeholders to prioritize use cases before a solution is designed.
whyWrong: Training comes later, once a solution exists.
Data migration follows design; it is not the purpose of discovery.
Sign-off happens after the solution is built and tested.

sampleQuestions.question: A consultant has finished building a new lead process in a sandbox. What should happen before go-live?
options: A direct rebuild of the changes in production
A full data export of every standard object
User acceptance testing with real sales users
An org-wide reset of all user passwords
sampleQuestions.explanation: User acceptance testing confirms that the process meets the business requirements for the people who will use it, before it is deployed to production.
whyWrong: Rebuilding by hand in production skips testing and invites errors.
A backup can be sensible, but it does not confirm that the process works for users.
Password resets have nothing to do with validating a new process.

sampleQuestions.question: A client is moving 300 reps from spreadsheets to Salesforce. Which plan best supports the change?
options: A single all-hands email sent out on the morning of the go-live date
Admin-only training, with reps expected to learn on the job
A written manual sent to reps one quarter after the launch
Role-based training, clear communication, and named champions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Change management combines a communication plan, training matched to each role, and local champions who help colleagues after launch.
whyWrong: One late announcement gives reps no time to prepare.
Reps are the main users and need training that fits their role.
Support that arrives months after launch is too late to help adoption.

sampleQuestions.question: Opportunity sharing is Private. A sales engineer needs edit access to one deal owned by a rep. What is the simplest option?
options: Add the engineer to the Opportunity Team
Change the org-wide default to Public Read/Write
Move the engineer above the rep in the role hierarchy
Transfer ownership of the deal to the engineer
sampleQuestions.explanation: An Opportunity Team gives named users a role and a level of access on a single Opportunity without changing the wider sharing model.
whyWrong: That opens every Opportunity to everyone, far beyond the one deal.
A role change would expose all of the rep's records, not one deal.
The rep still owns the deal; the engineer only needs to collaborate on it.

sampleQuestions.question: A company sells in several currencies and needs closed deals to keep the exchange rate from their close date. What should the consultant enable?
options: A separate price book for each currency the company uses
Advanced currency management with dated exchange rates
A formula field that converts each amount at today's rate
A custom Opportunity record type for each sales region
sampleQuestions.explanation: Advanced currency management adds dated exchange rates, so an Opportunity is converted at the rate that applied on its close date.
whyWrong: Price books hold prices; they do not preserve the exchange rate that applied on a close date.
A formula at today's rate would change historical amounts whenever the rate moves.
Record types control processes and layouts, not currency conversion.

sampleQuestions.question: A company sells the same products at different prices to retail and wholesale customers. What should the consultant set up?
options: A duplicate product record for each price point
A separate sales process for each customer type
A custom price book for each customer segment
A validation rule on the Opportunity amount field
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom price books let one product carry different list prices for different markets, channels, or customer segments.
whyWrong: Duplicating products splits reporting; one product can carry several prices through price books.
A sales process controls stages, not prices.
A validation rule checks data; it does not supply segment prices.

sampleQuestions.question: After conversion, a custom Lead field's value is missing from the new Contact. What is the likely cause?
options: The Lead was converted without creating an Opportunity
The Contact page layout uses a different record type
The Lead owner did not have a role in the hierarchy
The custom field was not mapped in lead field mapping
sampleQuestions.explanation: Standard Lead fields map automatically, but each custom Lead field must be mapped to a custom field on the Account, Contact, or Opportunity for its value to carry over.
whyWrong: Skipping the Opportunity does not stop field values reaching the Contact.
A layout affects what is displayed, not whether a value was copied.
The owner's role does not affect which field values carry over.

sampleQuestions.question: A team is loading legacy sales data. Which load order keeps relationships intact?
options: Accounts, then Contacts, then Opportunities
Opportunities, then Contacts, then Accounts
Contacts, then Opportunities, then Accounts
Opportunities, then Accounts, then Contacts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Parent records are loaded first. Contacts and Opportunities look up to Accounts, so Accounts go in before either of them.
whyWrong: Opportunities and Contacts both need their Account to exist first.
Contacts cannot be linked to Accounts that have not been loaded yet.
Opportunities need their Account to exist before they are loaded.

sampleQuestions.question: Reps keep creating Accounts that already exist. Which features work together to flag or block this?
options: Validation rules and sharing rules
Matching rules and duplicate rules
Assignment rules and escalation rules
Record types and page layouts
sampleQuestions.explanation: A matching rule defines how records are compared, and a duplicate rule decides whether to alert the user or block the save when a match is found.
whyWrong: Validation rules check field values and sharing rules open access; neither compares records for duplicates.
These route and escalate records; they do not detect duplicates.
These control processes and what users see, not duplicate detection.

sampleQuestions.question: Reps want to know which Leads to call first, based on how similar Leads converted in the past. Which tool fits?
options: Lead auto-response rules
Campaign Influence
Einstein Lead Scoring
Web-to-Lead
sampleQuestions.explanation: Einstein Lead Scoring is predictive AI. It scores each Lead by how closely it resembles Leads that converted before.
whyWrong: Auto-response rules send replies; they do not rank Leads.
Campaign Influence credits campaigns for Opportunities; it does not rank Leads.
Web-to-Lead captures Leads from a website form; it does not rank them.

sampleQuestions.question: Which task is an example of generative AI in a sales team's daily work?
options: Scoring each Opportunity by its likelihood of closing
Routing new Leads to queues by country and industry
Rolling up forecast amounts through the role hierarchy
Drafting a follow-up email grounded in CRM record data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Generative AI creates new content, such as a draft email or a call summary. Predictive AI estimates outcomes, such as a score.
whyWrong: Scoring is predictive AI: it estimates an outcome rather than creating content.
Rule-based routing is automation, not AI-generated content.
A forecast rollup is a calculation, not generated content.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales leader wants to use AI scores to decide which customers get discounts. Which step reflects Salesforce's Trusted AI principles?
options: Check the model for bias and keep a person in the decision
Hide from reps and customers that a score is being used
Apply the score automatically with no way to override it
Add fields such as age and gender to sharpen the score
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce's Trusted AI principles include being responsible, accountable, and transparent. Checking for bias and keeping human oversight apply them to a sales decision.
whyWrong: Transparency is one of the principles; hiding the use of AI works against it.
Removing human oversight works against accountability.
Sensitive attributes can introduce bias into the model.
